extracted.intended_audience: authors, publicists, PR professionals, and marketers creating book press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, formatting, and distributing press releases specifically announcing new books (including launches, editions, and book-signing events). Focuses on content, timing, format, audience targeting, and distribution tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show why readers will find the book exciting
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the journalist why their readers will find the book exciting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the announcement around why the audience should care — link the story to readers' interests to entice media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide main points while leaving readers wanting more
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the main points of the book while leaving the reader wanting more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a taste (high-level points) but avoid spoilers; the goal is to intrigue rather than fully summarize the plot or contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific logistical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific details like the release date and book signing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide release/purchase dates, event dates/locations, and links to pre-order channels so journalists and readers can act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of the press release
rubrics_metrics.description: You can write a book launch announcement whenever a book is newly-published and will be available for purchase within a few weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protip: write a new book press release several weeks before the book launch date, ideally when a pre-order sales channel is set up. You may also wait until the book is officially available if the release date is very recent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the standard press release format
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a standard expected format for press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While content can be creative, structure should follow basic rules so journalists get information in the format they expect. The article lists common elements (headline, subheader/lead, dateline, body, quote, company info, logo, media contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: A great headline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a strong, newsworthy headline that captures the angle and entices journalists to read further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheader / Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Subheader / Lead
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a subheader or lead to summarize the most important angle or hook immediately after the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the dateline (city and date) to orient journalists on timing and locality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Body
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write concise, well-structured paragraphs that combine storytelling with pertinent facts (no spoilers), focusing on genre, themes, and benefits to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include either a quote from the book or an endorsement quote; this is also a good spot to showcase book reviews or blurbs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company / Publisher info
rubrics_metrics.description: Company info
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide publisher name and brief company/publisher background as appropriate; place the publishing house prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Logo
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the publisher/organization logo to make the release look professional and brand-recognizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Media contact info
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't forget to include contact details — they are vital for follow-up. Provide a named contact, email, phone, and any PR representative details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find an interesting news angle / hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Find an interesting news angle; identify your hook and connect the book to current events, viral topics, Google Trends, and popular topics on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the book to timely themes or trends to grab journalists' attention; make the release a news story, not just an advertisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the book title immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the book title right away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't bury the title — put it prominently near the top so journalists and readers know what the release is about immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide book release/purchase details and links
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details on when and where the book will be made available for purchase; give links to pre-order channels if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for readers to buy or pre-order by including direct links and retailer/platform information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a brief summary focused on genre, themes, and reader benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief introduction to the book that focuses on high-level points like genre and themes, then include the benefits to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what readers will gain (education, escapism, new outlook) rather than just recounting plot; short, engaging paragraphs are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use quotes and endorsements strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: You can either include a quote from the book or use an endorsement quote; this is a great spot to showcase book reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether an in-text quote or external endorsement best supports your angle; include notable review snippets if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a brief author bio
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief bio is expected in your book release announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background on the author, including relevant expertise (especially important for self-help or nonfiction) and previous credits that lend credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: List publisher prominently
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the name of the publishing house prominently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps journalists identify the source and may influence perceived authority and distribution reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include awards or accolades if available
rubrics_metrics.description: If available, list the awards and accolades the author or the book have received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accolades to boost credibility — include award names, year, and granting organizations where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Call to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Call To Action: What do you want to happen after someone reads your press release?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit (purchase, pre-order, RSVP for event) and include links or instructions; make conversion as frictionless as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide high-quality visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a visual for the journalist to use in their article. Provide a high-quality photo of the author or the book cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach downloadable, high-resolution images and specify usage rights to make it easier for outlets to publish coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book-signing / event press release specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Your book signing press release should include all the event details, like the dates and locations, plus any pre-signing readings or interviews. Name all special guests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write separate press releases for each local event because each is a potential local news story pitched to different journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain author qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the author qualified to discuss this topic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially for advice-driven books, state why readers should trust the author (credentials, experience, prior work) rather than relying only on emotional angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain benefits to the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: What benefits does the book provide to the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the reader's perspective, clarify what they will gain: laughter, education, a new outlook, or actionable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the problem the book solves
rubrics_metrics.description: What problems does the book solve?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For guides/self-help, describe the current problem or aspiration readers have and explain how the book addresses it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear key messages for press/AI drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter key messages (Unique Selling Point, Author's Credibility, Target Audience and Appeal) when using tools or drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about USP, credibility, and who will care; the guide lists example key messages to feed AI or to structure the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Selling Point (USP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly articulate what makes your book stand out from others (compelling storyline, unique perspective, expert insights, timely topic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the USP prominent early in the release so journalists immediately grasp what differentiates your book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author's credibility / expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight the author's qualifications, experience, or relevant expertise that lend authority to the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use credentials, professional roles, previous publications, or lived experience to establish trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the intended audience and explain why the book will resonate with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify demographic, interest groups, or niches and tie the book's themes to those audiences to help journalists understand fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and answer follow-up questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional details so journalists don't need to ask many follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prowly's AI asks ten follow-up questions to complete drafts — proactively include likely journalist queries (availability, exclusives, embargoes, interview availability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customize and edit the draft to fit audience and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Customize and edit the press release draft: adjust header font styles, fine-tune content, adjust length, and cater it into a format you're happy with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor language and length to the target outlet (consumer blog vs. trade press) and use editing tools or human review to polish tone and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution via curated media database
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching your press release with a high-quality media database is the ideal scenario with the highest likelihood of capturing media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter contacts by beat and location, curate lists of journalists who cover books, and reach out individually with tailored pitches rather than mass blasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid buying one-off media lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Buying a media contact list is not recommended because one-off media outlet lists are notorious for being outdated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: purchased lists often have high bounce rates and lead to frustration; prefer up-to-date, filtered databases or in-house researcher work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with wire services for book releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a wire service to distribute your press release is often too broad of a pitch for book releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services can be too general; you're more likely to get results by curating outlets and sending tailored pitches to journalists individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share with aligned local partners
rubrics_metrics.description: To reach target audiences, share the press release with local businesses or nonprofit organizations that align with the book's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating partnerships can expand reach and provide local hooks for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add press releases to your online newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a PR software tool, don’t forget to add new press releases to your online newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An online newsroom centralizes releases for journalists and can serve as a resource for media outreach and archival purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PR tools to get journalist recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use software like Prowly to receive contact recommendations for journalists based on keywords found in your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools can suggest journalists who cover similar topics; further research is recommended to check what they've covered recently and tailor the pitch.
